scope: Maintainer read-only observation of one physical Android phone; no personal AI task was executed in this window.
preconditions_and_interventions: The original pairing and phone accounts were retained during the upgrade.
After upgrade, the accessibility permission remained configured but the operation service was not bound. The recovery carrier started; this did not restore device control by itself.
The maintainer enabled Flyme background and associated startup settings through system UI, then toggled the accessibility service off and on and confirmed the system permission dialog.
The original connection resumed after that manual intervention. This is not an autonomous upgrade recovery pass.
The maintainer returned HOME and requested screen sleep before observation. No phone UI actions or upgrade were issued by this test during the observation window.

observation.method: Read-only adb pidof/dumpsys sampling, approximately every 30 seconds, with a separate final sample; diagnostic log readback after the interruption.
observation.wake_event: PowerManagerService recorded WAKE_REASON_POWER_BUTTON at 23:50:43.033. The event does not identify who initiated it.

conclusions: The process and operation-service binding persisted in every collected sample.
The screen woke after approximately 50 minutes, so this is not a full 60-minute uninterrupted idle pass.
Dozing is a screen wakefulness state here; device idle mode was false. This does not verify deep Doze or unpowered endurance.
No Muse or Instinct autonomous wake, SMS GUI, cross-app task, network recovery, or subsequent-use result is established by these samples.
This candidate observation does not change the public recommended APK or establish readiness to replace another phone's existing control path.
privacy: This record was manually reduced to version, timing, diagnostic classifications and outcomes. Raw phone/system evidence remains private; no phone serial, account, message content or pairing credential is included.
